newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crude prices rise amid quiet market.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crude prices rise amid quiet market.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices rose Monday, traders said, attributing the higher values to strength in other regional market.
Meanwhile, West Coast trade was thin, with most refiners finished with July business last week.
Higher volumes of imports, weak refinery margins out West, and excess sellers have weakend regional buying interest, traders said.
With discounts unchanged, the regional benchmark, Alaska North Slope (ANS), rose in sympathy with higher prices for WTI.
The grade's main seller, BP, offered cargoes at $1.85 under July deliveries of WTI, the U.S basis for cash and futures oil markets.
Outright prices for ANS were $16.64/16.84 a barrel, up 30 cents for the second-straight day.
Heavier California grades were flat Monday after falling late last week with lower postings.
